values: Use « finir de + infinitif » for finishing an action, and « finir par + infinitif » for eventually doing something.
Besides flambéing food, « flamber » can mean to blaze or, figuratively, for prices to rise sharply.
The injury sense is most often pronominal: « se fouler la cheville » means to sprain one’s ankle.
Use « frapper à la porte » for knocking on a door, but direct-object « frapper quelqu’un ou quelque chose » for hitting someone or something.
« Fredonner » means to sing a tune quietly with the mouth partly closed, often without words.
« Fuir » can be intransitive (“to flee”) or take a direct object meaning to avoid or flee from it.
Use « féliciter quelqu’un pour quelque chose » to congratulate someone on an achievement or event.
Transitive « goûter quelque chose » means to taste or try it; « goûter à » can mean to experience or sample something.

batch_summary: Added missing senses and notes on complements, pronominal use, and figurative meanings.
